cantileverBeam.explanation: Assess a rectangular structural member under six signed end resultants: axial force, biaxial bending forces, end torque and biaxial bending couples. Inputs describe physical intent and serviceability, while Schemaxis generates quadratic solid meshes and independently checks axial/Euler-Bernoulli/Prandtl theory, support equilibrium, separate refinement and exact saved-deck readback. Clamped members permit combined loads; axialSlide permits only axial loads while allowing Poisson contraction. Outputs are beam.inp, interior-stress.csv and beam-assessment.json. Choose this for bounded linear elastic stiffness and sampled-stress studies.
pitfalls: Only one straight solid rectangular section family; no arbitrary meshes/decks, nonlinearity, buckling, thermal, modal, contact or failure analysis.
Interior sampled stress excludes the clamp/loaded end and does not bound peak stress or certify yielding.
Cancelling forces/couples can yield almost zero translation with nonzero stress; absolute-contribution scales preserve numerical checks.
A numerically valid solve can fail explicit serviceability requirements.

examples.purpose: All six resultants with measured translation, twist and sampled von Mises limits.
Pure axial compression with transverse contraction.

fields.explanation: A rectangular isotropic linear elastic member study in SI units. Declare dimensions, material, six optional signed end resultants, a support, mesh controls and measured serviceability limits. Schemaxis derives meshes, checks independent axial/bending/torsion theory and equilibrium, then publishes a checked editable deck, interior stress table and assessment. Unspecified load components are zero; at least one resultant must be nonzero.

/properties/version.explanation: Format identifier of this Schemaxis document; it must be "schemaxis.calculix/1". It is separate from the CalculiX solver release (the adaptor targets CalculiX 2.23).

/properties/operation.explanation: cantileverBeam generates and assesses the supported rectangular structural-member family. The retained operation name includes pure axial members and combined biaxial bending/torsion. It covers one clamped support or pure-axial sliding support; it does not accept arbitrary solver decks.

/properties/beam.explanation: Straight solid rectangular geometry in metres. The member spans x=0 to x=length; its section is centred on y=z=0. Width is along y and height along z. Only rectangular solid sections are supported; changing either dimension also changes axial and torsional stiffness.

/properties/beam/properties/length_m.explanation: Distance between supported and loaded faces along positive x, in metres. For fixed section and loads, bending-force deflection grows as length cubed, bending-couple deflection as length squared, axial extension and torsional twist as length. Slenderness length/max(width,height) must stay between 20 and 40.

/properties/beam/properties/width_m.explanation: Full rectangle size along y, in metres. This dimension enters axial area linearly, bending stiffness for a y force cubically, bending stiffness for a z force linearly, and the rectangular torsion constant. Width/height must remain 0.5..2.

/properties/beam/properties/height_m.explanation: Full rectangle size along z, in metres. Bending stiffness for a z force scales with height cubed; height also changes axial area and torsional compliance. This is the full height, not the half-distance from centre to surface.

/properties/material.explanation: Uniform isotropic linear elastic material defined by Young's modulus and Poisson's ratio. There is no yield law, temperature dependence, damage or failure assessment.

/properties/material/properties/youngsMo.explanation: Young's modulus E in Pa, 1e6..1e12; examples are 2.1e11 for steel and 7e10 for aluminium. Doubling E at fixed Poisson ratio halves axial/bending translations and torsional twist under the same prescribed resultants, while interior stress remains load-controlled. This declares elasticity, not yield strength.
pitfalls: Enter pascals, not GPa or MPa: 210 GPa is 210000000000.

/properties/material/properties/poissonR.explanation: Dimensionless isotropic lateral contraction ratio, 0..0.35. Together with E it sets shear modulus G=E/[2(1+nu)], so it affects torsional twist directly. A clamped end inhibits local contraction; axialSlide permits it for pure axial loads. No material yielding or buckling model is supplied.

/properties/load.explanation: Six global end-face resultants, with omitted components defaulting to zero: forces in N and moments in N m. Transverse forces, axial force and end couples can be superposed for clamped members. Right-hand-rule moments are distributed consistent face tractions; solid nodes have no rotational degrees of freedom. Equal/opposite contributions may cancel tip translation but still produce stress. At least one force or moment/length must reach 0.01 N.

/properties/load/properties/tipForceZ_N.explanation: Transverse end force along z: positive force bends towards positive z, about the y axis. Units are N; omission means zero. Force and end-moment contributions add according to their signed directions; each nonzero active translation is checked against an absolute-contribution theory scale.

/properties/mesh.explanation: Base resolution of the quadratic 20-node brick mesh. The second mesh doubles axial cells and the fine mesh doubles all directions. Every active translation and twist must change by at most 1% of its absolute-contribution theory scale on each independent refinement; fine responses must agree within 3% of theory.

/properties/mesh/properties/lengthCells.explanation: Number of base mesh elements along the beam length, 12 to 24. The axially refined and fine meshes use twice this number. The element length divided by the smallest section cell must not exceed 10.
pitfalls: More cells do not guarantee acceptance; NUMERICAL_ACCEPTANCE_FAILED means the refinement or theory check failed and the measured changes are reported.

/properties/mesh/properties/sectionCells.explanation: Number of base mesh elements across each of the width and height, 2 or 3. The fine mesh doubles this in both directions, exposing any error from too coarse a section.

/properties/requirements.explanation: Up to 16 uniquely named upper limits on actual native measurements. Translation components/magnitude, torsional twist and interior sampled normal/von Mises stress are available. Omission means no user limit, while independent numerical acceptance still applies. An unmet limit retains measured margins but blocks publication and workflow reuse.

/properties/requirements/items.explanation: One named limit: a measured quantity and its nonnegative maximum. The measured value passes when it is less than or equal to the maximum; no safety factor or tolerance is added.

/properties/requirements/items/propertie.explanation: Unique name for this limit, used in the assessment report: a lowercase letter followed by up to 63 lowercase letters, digits or underscores.

Choose absTipAreaMeanUx_m, absTipAreaMeanUy_m or absTipAreaMeanUz_m for absolute area-mean component translation, tipAreaMeanTranslation_m for that mean vector magnitude, absTipTwist_rad for the absolute area-moment torsional rotation, maxInteriorSampleNormalStress_Pa for absolute Sxx, or maxInteriorSampleVonMises_Pa for the equivalent stress of actual interior Gauss samples. Samples lie in 0.3<=x/L<=0.7; neither stress quantity bounds peak/root/surface stress or proves yield/fatigue safety.

Nonnegative inclusive upper bound in the chosen quantity's units: m for translation, rad for twist and Pa for sampled stress. For example 0.0004 m or 0.00025 rad. A measured value above the bound causes PERFORMANCE_NOT_MET; the adaptor never adjusts this limit automatically.

/properties/load/properties/tipForceX_N.explanation: Axial end force: positive tension extends the member and negative compression shortens it. Compression does not establish buckling stability. Units are N; omission means zero. Force and end-moment contributions add according to their signed directions; each nonzero active translation is checked against an absolute-contribution theory scale.

/properties/load/properties/tipForceY_N.explanation: Transverse end force along y: positive force bends towards positive y, about the z axis. Units are N; omission means zero. Force and end-moment contributions add according to their signed directions; each nonzero active translation is checked against an absolute-contribution theory scale.

/properties/load/properties/tipMomentX_N.explanation: End torque about positive x by the right-hand rule: positive torque rotates the positive-y edge towards positive z. Its measured area-moment twist is compared with rectangular Saint-Venant torsion theory. Units are N m; omission means zero. The moment acts about the centre of the loaded face and is realised by distributed nodal forces.
/properties/load/properties/tipMomentX_N.defaultMeaning: No end couple about this axis.

/properties/load/properties/tipMomentY_N.explanation: End bending couple about positive y: positive moment bends the loaded face towards negative z. It contributes -My*L^2/(2*E*Iy) to tip z translation. Units are N m; omission means zero. The moment acts about the centre of the loaded face and is realised by distributed nodal forces.
/properties/load/properties/tipMomentY_N.defaultMeaning: No end couple about this axis.

/properties/load/properties/tipMomentZ_N.explanation: End bending couple about positive z: positive moment bends the loaded face towards positive y. It contributes Mz*L^2/(2*E*Iz) to tip y translation. Units are N m; omission means zero. The moment acts about the centre of the loaded face and is realised by distributed nodal forces.
/properties/load/properties/tipMomentZ_N.defaultMeaning: No end couple about this axis.

/properties/support.explanation: clamped (default) fixes all translations of the x=0 face and accepts all six resultants. axialSlide fixes axial translation there and restrains transverse motion only along the section symmetry lines, permitting uniform Poisson contraction. axialSlide accepts only a nonzero axial force; it is not a simply-supported bending or arbitrary roller model.
